Apple___Apple_scab.name: Apple Scab
symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves
Spots turn dark and scabby with age
actions: Remove and destroy infected leaves
Rake up and destroy fallen leaves to break the infection cycle
Prune the canopy to improve airflow and drying
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Apply a locally approved protectant fungicide (e.g. captan or mancozeb) from green-tip to petal fall, following the label schedule
prevention: Clean up leaf litter every autumn

favourable.note: Cool, wet spring weather with long leaf-wetness periods

Apple___Black_rot.name: Black Rot
symptoms: 'Frog-eye' leaf spots: tan centres with purple margins
actions: Prune out dead wood and cankered branches
Remove mummified fruit from the tree and ground
Remove infected leaves
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Apply a locally approved fungicide (e.g. captan) during the growing season
prevention: Keep the orchard free of prunings and fruit mummies

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.name: Cedar Apple Rust
symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf surface
Small tube-like structures under the spots
actions: Remove infected leaves
Remove galls from nearby juniper / cedar trees (the alternate host)
Monitor neighbouring trees
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Apply a locally approved fungicide (e.g. myclobutanil) from pink bud stage

Background_without_leaves.name: No leaf detected
Background_without_leaves.cause: The image does not contain a recognisable crop leaf

Cherry___Powdery_mildew.name: Powdery Mildew
actions: Prune out infected shoots
Improve airflow through the canopy
Avoid excess nitrogen fertiliser
Cherry___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Apply sulphur, potassium bicarbonate or another locally approved fungicide
prevention: Prune annually for an open canopy
Water at the base, not over the leaves

Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_sp.name: Gray Leaf Spot
symptoms: Rectangular tan to grey lesions bounded by leaf veins
Lesions merge and blight whole leaves
actions: Rotate with a non-host crop next season
Bury or manage infected crop residue
Monitor upper leaves before tasselling
Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_sp.treatment: If lesions reach the upper leaves before tasselling, apply a locally approved foliar fungicide (strobilurin / triazole)
prevention: Avoid continuous maize on the same field

favourable.note: Warm, very humid weather with long dew periods

Corn___Common_rust.name: Common Rust
symptoms: Cinnamon-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces
Pustules turn black late in the season
actions: Monitor pustule spread on upper leaves
Remove heavily infected leaves in small plots
Keep fertilisation balanced
Corn___Common_rust.treatment: On susceptible hybrids with early, heavy infection, apply a locally approved foliar fungicide
prevention: Plant early to escape peak infection

Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.name: Northern Leaf Blight
symptoms: Long cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions
actions: Rotate crops and manage infected residue
Monitor upper leaves around tasselling
Remove severely infected leaves in small plots
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment: If disease reaches the ear leaf before silking, apply a locally approved foliar fungicide

Grape___Black_rot.name: Black Rot
symptoms: Circular tan leaf spots with dark brown borders
Tiny black dots (fruiting bodies) in the spots
Berries shrivel into hard black mummies
actions: Remove mummified berries and infected leaves
Prune to open the canopy
Keep the vineyard floor clean
Grape___Black_rot.treatment: Apply a locally approved fungicide (e.g. mancozeb or myclobutanil) from bud break to bunch closure
prevention: Remove all mummies during dormant pruning

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).name: Esca (Black Measles)
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).cause: Fungal trunk disease complex (Phaeomoniella / Phaeoacremonium spp.)
symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' yellow / red-brown discolouration between leaf veins
actions: Mark affected vines and monitor them each season
Prune out infected wood well below visible symptoms
Protect large pruning wounds
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment: There is no curative spray. Remove severely affected vines and protect pruning wounds with an approved wound sealant

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.name: Leaf Blight (Isariopsis Leaf Spot)
symptoms: Irregular dark brown spots on leaves
Spots merge and leaves dry out
actions: Remove infected leaves
Improve air circulation in the canopy
Monitor neighbouring vines
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.treatment: Apply a copper-based or other locally approved fungicide

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).name: Huanglongbing (Citrus Greening)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).cause: Bacterial infection (Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus) spread by the Asian citrus psyllid
symptoms: Blotchy, asymmetric yellow mottling of leaves
actions: Have the diagnosis confirmed by a lab or local agriculture officer
Control psyllid insects across the orchard
Remove and destroy confirmed infected trees to protect healthy ones
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).treatment: There is no cure. Control the psyllid vector with locally approved insecticides and remove infected trees
prevention: Plant only certified disease-free nursery stock
Inspect new flush regularly for psyllids

favourable.note: Warm weather that favours psyllid populations

Peach___Bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial Spot
symptoms: Small water-soaked angular leaf spots turning purple-brown
actions: Remove severely infected twigs and leaves
Avoid excess nitrogen
Avoid overhead irrigation
Peach___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply a copper-based bactericide at leaf fall and dormancy, as locally approved
prevention: Use windbreaks to reduce leaf injury

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial Spot
symptoms: Leaf drop and scabby fruit spots
actions: Remove infected leaves and badly affected plants
Avoid overhead irrigation and working with wet plants
Monitor neighbouring plants
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply a copper-based bactericide as locally approved
prevention: Rotate away from peppers and tomatoes for 2-3 years

favourable.note: Warm, wet weather and splashing rain

Potato___Early_blight.name: Early Blight
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric 'target' rings
actions: Remove severely affected lower leaves
Avoid overhead watering
Keep fertilisation balanced (stressed plants are more susceptible)
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Apply a locally approved protectant fungicide (e.g. chlorothalonil or mancozeb)
prevention: Destroy volunteer plants and crop debris

favourable.note: Warm weather with alternating wet and dry periods

Potato___Late_blight.name: Late Blight
symptoms: Pale green, water-soaked lesions turning dark brown
White mould on the leaf underside in humid weather
actions: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately (do not compost)
Avoid overhead irrigation
Inspect neighbouring plants daily - this disease spreads within days
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Apply a locally approved fungicide immediately (protectant such as mancozeb, or systemic such as metalaxyl / cymoxanil)
prevention: Harvest tubers in dry weather and destroy cull piles

Squash___Powdery_mildew.name: Powdery Mildew
symptoms: White powdery spots on leaves and stems
actions: Remove heavily infected leaves
Improve spacing and airflow
Water at the base of plants
Squash___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Apply sulphur, potassium bicarbonate, neem oil or another locally approved fungicide

favourable.note: Warm, dry days with humid nights

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.name: Leaf Scorch
symptoms: Small irregular purple spots on leaves
Spots merge; leaf looks burnt / scorched
actions: Remove infected leaves
Use drip irrigation instead of sprinklers
Renovate beds after harvest
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.treatment: Apply a locally approved fungicide (e.g. captan) during early growth

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial Spot
symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves
actions: Remove infected leaves and badly affected plants
Avoid overhead irrigation and handling wet plants
Monitor neighbouring plants
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply a copper-based bactericide (often with mancozeb) as locally approved
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants
Rotate away from tomato and pepper for 2-3 years

favourable.note: Warm, wet weather and splashing rain

Tomato___Early_blight.name: Early Blight
symptoms: Circular brown lesions with concentric rings
actions: Remove severely affected leaves
Avoid prolonged leaf wetness
Improve plant spacing and airflow
Monitor nearby plants
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Apply a locally approved fungicide (e.g. chlorothalonil or mancozeb)
prevention: Mulch to stop soil splashing onto leaves
Stake plants and rotate crops for 2-3 years

favourable.note: Warm, humid weather with long leaf wetness

Tomato___Late_blight.name: Late Blight
symptoms: Large greasy grey-green to brown lesions
White mould on the leaf underside in humid weather
actions: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately (do not compost)
Avoid overhead irrigation
Inspect neighbouring plants daily - this disease spreads within days
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment: Apply a locally approved fungicide immediately (protectant such as mancozeb, or systemic such as metalaxyl / cymoxanil)

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.name: Leaf Mold
symptoms: Pale green / yellow spots on the upper leaf surface
Olive-green velvety mould on the underside
actions: Reduce humidity - ventilate greenhouses / polyhouses
Remove infected leaves
Increase plant spacing
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment: Apply a locally approved fungicide if humidity cannot be controlled

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.name: Septoria Leaf Spot
symptoms: Many small circular spots with dark borders and grey centres
Tiny black dots inside the spots
actions: Remove infected lower leaves
Mulch to stop soil splash
Avoid overhead watering
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Apply a locally approved fungicide (e.g. chlorothalonil or copper)

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.name: Spider Mite Damage
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.cause: Pest infestation (two-spotted spider mite, Tetranychus urticae)
symptoms: Fine yellow / white stippling on leaves
Fine webbing on the leaf underside
actions: Inspect the undersides of leaves
Remove heavily infested portions
Spray plants with a strong jet of water to dislodge mites
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment: Use neem oil or insecticidal soap; if severe, apply a locally approved miticide. Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural predators
prevention: Release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis) where available
Avoid water stress - mites thrive on dry, stressed plants

Tomato___Target_Spot.name: Target Spot
symptoms: Lesions can merge and blight leaves
actions: Remove infected lower leaves
Improve airflow by pruning and staking
Avoid overhead irrigation
Tomato___Target_Spot.treatment: Apply a locally approved fungicide (e.g. chlorothalonil or azoxystrobin)

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Viral infection (TYLCV) spread by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci)
actions: Uproot infected plants, bag them and destroy away from the field
Control whiteflies with yellow sticky traps
Monitor neighbouring plants for new curling
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment: There is no cure for the virus. Control the whitefly vector with neem oil or a locally approved insecticide

favourable.note: Warm weather that favours whitefly populations

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.name: Tomato Mosaic Virus
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Viral infection (ToMV), spread by contact, tools and seed
symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic pattern
actions: Remove and destroy infected plants
Disinfect hands and tools after handling plants
Do not use tobacco products near plants
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: There is no cure. Prevent spread through hygiene and removal of infected plants

N.name: Nitrogen (N) deficiency
actions: Confirm with a soil or leaf-tissue test before applying fertiliser
Apply nitrogen (urea, ammonium sulphate or well-rotted compost) as per soil-test advice
Split the dose across the season to reduce losses

K.name: Potassium (K) deficiency
actions: Confirm with a soil or leaf-tissue test
Apply potash (muriate or sulphate of potash) as per soil-test advice
Ensure adequate soil moisture so roots can take up potassium

Fe/Mg.name: Iron (Fe) or Magnesium (Mg) deficiency
signature: Yellowing between leaf veins while veins stay green
actions: Confirm with a soil or leaf-tissue test, and check soil pH (high pH locks up iron)
Iron: foliar spray of chelated iron or ferrous sulphate
Magnesium: foliar spray or soil application of magnesium sulphate (Epsom salt)
No visible abnormality detected
Continue routine weekly monitoring
Maintain balanced irrigation and fertilisation
Re-scan if new spots, yellowing or curling appear
